primary_meaning: In mainstream Christian teaching, 'living water' primarily symbolizes the Holy Spirit given by Jesus Christ to believers, and closely bound up with that, the eternal life / salvation that Christ offers. Jesus is presented as the source of this water, which quenches spiritual thirst permanently and wells up to eternal life. John's Gospel itself supplies the dominant interpretive key by stating that the rivers of living water refer to the Spirit whom believers would receive.
primary_basis: John 4:10-14 (Jesus and the Samaritan woman: 'living water... welling up to eternal life')
John 7:37-39 (rivers of living water; the evangelist's explicit gloss: 'this he said about the Spirit')
Jeremiah 2:13 and 17:13 (God as 'the fountain of living waters')
Zechariah 14:8 (living waters flowing out from Jerusalem)
Isaiah 12:3; 44:3; 55:1 (water/Spirit poured out; drawing water from the wells of salvation)
Revelation 7:17; 21:6; 22:1, 22:17 (the water of life, the river of the water of life)
Ezekiel 47:1-12 (river flowing from the temple, widely read typologically)

alternatives.meaning: The Holy Spirit specifically (as distinct from eternal life generally) — many commentators treat John 7:39 as fixing the referent exclusively as the Spirit.
Eternal life / salvation itself, or Christ and his saving revelation as the gift, with the Spirit as a secondary or mediated referent (a classic exegetical debate on John 4).

The literal Hebrew idiom mayim chayyim, meaning fresh, flowing (spring) water as opposed to stagnant cistern water — the linguistic base on which the symbolism trades; in ritual contexts it refers to water suitable for purification.
Baptism / baptismal regeneration — a sacramental reading prominent in patristic, Catholic, and Orthodox interpretation, and in early church practice ('baptize in living water,' Didache 7).
The word of God / the gospel or divine teaching that cleanses and gives life (a homiletical extension found in some Protestant preaching and older commentary).

Wisdom or Torah as living water — the Jewish background tradition (Sirach, Qumran, rabbinic sources) sometimes invoked by scholars as the frame Jesus reworks; occasionally carried into Christian readings as 'divine wisdom/revelation.'

notes: There is a recognizable, well-settled consensus: living water symbolizes the Spirit and the eternal life Christ gives, largely because John 7:39 provides an inner-biblical interpretation. The main live debate within the consensus is whether the referent in John 4 is the Spirit, eternal life, Christ's revelation, or all of these together; most commentators treat these as overlapping rather than competing. The literal idiom (flowing spring water) is universally acknowledged as the semantic background rather than a rival symbolic meaning. Sacramental (baptismal) readings are tradition-dependent: common in Catholic/Orthodox and patristic sources, less emphasized in evangelical Protestant interpretation.
